feature1.prompt: Using multiple FilteredRelation with different filters but for the same relation is ignored. In the current behavior, even when there is always at least one entry with is_all=True and optionally another entry with a zone-specific filter, the query only generates a single SQL JOIN. This means that the intended logic of using FilteredRelation together with Case(When()) to choose between a zone-specific value and a fallback 'All' value fails because the additional filtered relation is silently ignored. The fix must ensure that each FilteredRelation with a distinct filter produces its own join so that both conditions can be evaluated correctly.
feature1.hint_texts: Enhance the core join logic in the ORM by modifying the join method to accept a new parameter 'reuse_with_filtered_relation'. Update the build_filter, build_filtered_relation_q, and setup_joins functions to propagate this parameter. This change must prevent improper alias reuse when multiple FilteredRelation instances for the same underlying relation are present.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/models/sql/query.py; functions to modify include join (modify the join method signature and its reuse logic), build_filter (add and pass reuse_with_filtered_relation), build_filtered_relation_q (ensure the new parameter is enforced), and setup_joins (update to handle the new parameter correctly).

feature2.prompt: The new functionality needs to be validated by ensuring that multiple FilteredRelation usages on the same relation generate distinct SQL JOINs. After the fix, when applying different filters—one for a zone-specific condition and another for the is_all flag—the query should properly annotate the results so that the zone-level data is used when available, and the fallback is used otherwise. This verification will ensure that the query created using Case(When()) reflects the proper join logic and returns the expected output. The test should check that both filtered relations are correctly handled and that no join is inadvertently ignored.
feature2.hint_texts: Introduce a new test case (for example, test_multiple) in the tests/filtered_relation/tests.py file. This test should construct a query that uses two FilteredRelation annotations with different filter conditions on the same relation. The test must assert that the returned SQL contains two separate JOINs and that the query correctly selects between the zone-specific data and the fallback 'All' data.
feature2.entrypoint: File: tests/filtered_relation/tests.py; add a new test function (test_multiple) within the appropriate test class (e.g., FilteredRelationTests) to validate that multiple FilteredRelation instances work as expected.
